feedback: Iteration 1 (entityR2B, 111.80) showed that the 0.06 m sensor span removed line loss: it fell from 1 to 0 per run on oval and s-bend, and to 0.1 on slalom. Iteration 2 (entityR2A geometry with kp 4 and kd 0.6, 114.36) kept that geometry and changed the controller. It did not reduce max_error, which stayed at 0.063 to 0.064 m on all tracks. It also raised line loss to 0.25 on oval and 0.30 on slalom, and raised s-bend oscillation to 0.28. Progress on oval fell from 0.55 to 0.32. I read this as the controller overshooting near the sensor edge, not as a geometry fault, so I am reducing gain rather than changing the platform. Because the geometry is held, I am not asking for changes now. For the next race, the question is whether the controller alone brings line loss back to near zero. If line loss on oval or slalom stays at 0.2 or more, the sensor y or inertia change is the cause, so revert sensor y to 0.03 first, keeping mass at 0.7. If line loss returns near zero but max_error stays at 0.063 m, the limit is bend speed and track width, so try wheel_track 0.10 next, since it gives more turn rate per unit of wheel differential. If neither is the cause, the array is not the limit, so I would not add sensors.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration-2 geometry for this race (sensor y 0.02, body_length 0.14, mass 0.7, ±0.06 m span with 16 mm footprints) so the controller change is isolated.
If line_loss_events is still 0.2 or higher on oval or slalom after this race, revert sensor y to 0.03 while keeping mass 0.7 and body_length 0.14.
If line loss returns near 0 but max_error stays at about 0.063 m, try wheel_track 0.10 to increase turn rate per unit of wheel differential.
